chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki, who said: Jadh'an ibn Nasr Abu Nasr al-Kandi narrated to me, Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him)

about His Word, the Mighty and High: 'And His Throne was upon the Water.' He said to me: 'What do they say about this?' I said: 'They say that the Throne was upon the water, and the Lord was above it.' He said: 'They have lied. Whoever claims this has made Allah a bearer and described Him with the attribute of the created, and it necessarily follows that the thing which carries Him is stronger than He is.' I said: 'Clarify for me, may I be your ransom,'

then he said: 'Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, burdened the water with His Knowledge and His Religion before there was earth or sky, or jinn or man, or sun or moon. When He intended to create the creation, He scattered them before Him and said to them: 'Who is your Lord?' The first to speak were the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and the Imams (peace be upon them). They said: 'You are our Lord.' So He bore them with Knowledge and Religion,'

then He said to the angels: 'These are the bearers of My Knowledge and My Religion, and My Trustees in My creation, and they are the ones to be asked.' Then it was said to the children of Adam: 'Acknowledge the Lordship and obedience to these people.' They said: 'Yes, our Lord, we have acknowledged.' He said to the angels: 'Bear witness.' The angels said: 'We bear witness.'

Do they not say: 'Surely we were heedless of this' or: 'Only our fathers associated others (with Allah) before, and we were an offspring after them: Wilt Thou then destroy us for what the vain doers did?'
O Dawud, our guardianship (wilayah) is emphasized upon them in the covenant.

key_terms.الدِّينُ: Religion, the system of divine guidance
key_terms.الْعَرْشُ: The Throne, often interpreted metaphorically as divine authority or knowledge in this context
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: The Water, the primordial element upon which the Throne/Knowledge rested
key_terms.الْمِيثَاقُ: The Covenant, the pre-eternal agreement between God and the faithful
key_terms.الْوِلَايَةُ: Guardianship/Authority, the spiritual and temporal authority of the Imams
key_terms.عِلْمٌ: Knowledge, specifically divine knowledge entrusted to the Imams

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'His Throne was upon the Water' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the anthropomorphic view of Allah being physically carried by clarifying that He burdened the primordial water with His Knowledge and Religion before creation. He identifies the Prophet, the Imams, and Adam as the first to acknowledge this divine authority, establishing the pre-eternal covenant of Wilayah. This narration underscores the Shia doctrine of divine transcendence (tanzih) and the metaphysical role of the Imams as carriers of God's knowledge.
